raw_llm_output: For Well 15/9-F-9A, the risk of STUCK PIPE is currently CRITICAL, with a risk score of 0.8 and a 95% confidence interval between 0.4902 and 0.9433. The prediction is based on similar patterns found in 8 out of 10 offset wells, indicating that while most analogs experienced stuck pipe, two did not. Top analog wells such as SYNTH-W09 and SYNTH-W35 commonly encountered differential sticking events, often during stationary survey periods. [SNIPPET_SYNTH-W09_2011-01-20_STUCK_PIPE] [SNIPPET_SYNTH-W09_2010-01-25_STUCK_PIPE] [SNIPPET_SYNTH-W35_2011-04-08_STUCK_PIPE] These incidents occurred at various depths, for example, 1541.1m in SYNTH-W09 and 3747.0m in SYNTH-W35, and were typically resolved by spotting pipe-freeing fluid, working with maximum torque, and raising mud weight. [SNIPPET_SYNTH-W09_2011-01-20_STUCK_PIPE] [SNIPPET_SYNTH-W35_2011-04-08_STUCK_PIPE] [SNIPPET_SYNTH-W09_2010-01-25_STUCK_PIPE] Associated non-productive time for these events ranged from 4.9 hours to 10.9 hours. [SNIPPET_SYNTH-W09_2011-01-20_STUCK_PIPE] [SNIPPET_SYNTH-W26_2011-03-12_STUCK_PIPE] [SNIPPET_SYNTH-W35_2011-04-08_STUCK_PIPE] This is currently a monitoring alert and not yet actionable.
